title: The flower-to-seed investigation
subtitle: Trace pollen, fertilisation and the formation of seeds
objective: Describe pollination, fertilisation and seed formation as different connected processes.

sow.exactOutcome: Describe reproduction in plants (pollination, seed formation).
sow.alignment: New outcome; flowering-plant reproduction sequence. Original secondary-age exemplar at an upper-KS2 conceptual level; no qualification approval or completion claim.

priorLearning: Know that reproduction produces new individuals.
success: Trace pollen from anther to stigma.
Distinguish pollen transfer from fusion of gametes.
Explain that a fertilised ovule develops into a seed.

vocabulary.meaning: Grains that carry the male reproductive cells in flowering plants.
Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma.
The flower part that receives pollen.
A structure in the ovary containing an egg cell; it can develop into a seed.
Fusion of male and female gametes.
A reproductive cell such as an egg cell.

equipment: Shared orchard evidence, chosen route, pencils; optional paper pollen tokens.
preparation: Use diagrams or paper tokens, not real pollen.
Explain that our example follows ordinary sexual reproduction in a flowering plant.
safety: No pollen blowing, plant tasting or flower dissection is required; paper route avoids pollen allergy exposure.
practicalAlternative: Trace paper pollen and stage cards using the supplied observations. No live plant, internet or completed growing trial is needed.

misconceptions.claim: Pollination is the same as fertilisation.
misconceptions.correction: Pollination transfers pollen; fertilisation is gamete fusion later in the ovule.

misconceptions.claim: A pollen grain simply becomes a seed.
misconceptions.correction: A fertilised ovule develops into a seed; the pollen supplies male gametes.
misconceptions.check: Ask which structure develops into the seed.

misconceptions.claim: Every pollen grain landing anywhere on a plant makes a seed.
misconceptions.correction: Pollen must reach a suitable stigma; further processes and suitable conditions are needed.
misconceptions.check: Ask whether pollen on a leaf counts as pollination.

access.supported: Order named stages using prompts and label the main route.
access.standard: Explain the three processes and interpret an orchard evidence set.
access.stretch: Evaluate a pollination guarantee and explain limits of the observations.
access.regulation: Offer private writing, pointing, drawing or adult scribing. Allow pass-and-return for public questions and desk-based participation. Choose support from current learning evidence, not fixed ability labels.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e: Pollination and fertilization
sources.note: Checked September 2026. Pollination differs from gamete fusion; fertilised ovule develops into seed and ovary into fruit. College detail is selectively simplified for GROW.

slides.title: A pollen delivery mystery
body: Pollen reaches a plant. Does that guarantee a seed?
We will follow the destination and the next processes.
slides.notes: Invite predictions without requiring existing terminology. Explain that paper evidence gives the whole investigation.

slides.title: Recover the plant words
body: R1. Name a flowering-plant part.
R2. What can a seed grow into in suitable conditions?
R3. Does reproduction mean the parent grows taller?
slides.notes: Valid part; new plant; no, reproduction makes offspring, whereas growth increases size/development of an individual.

slides.title: I trace the correct delivery destination
body: Anthers produce pollen.
A stigma receives pollen.
Pollination names this transfer.
slides.notes: Think aloud: I place my token on the anther, then move it to the stigma. A landing on a leaf would not complete this defined transfer. This selected diagram omits petals and exact scale.

visual.title: Selected flower structures and pollen transfer
visual.description: A simplified flower section labels anther, pollen, stigma, style, ovary and ovule. A pollen-transfer arrow goes from anther to stigma; it does not lead directly to a seed.

elements.text: Selected structures only; not to scale. Petals are omitted.

slides.title: I distinguish the event inside the ovule
body: Compatible pollen can grow a tube.
A male gamete reaches an egg cell.
Their fusion is fertilisation.
slides.notes: Shared I do time. Think aloud: The transfer has already happened; now I describe a different event. The male gamete travels through a tube; the egg is in an ovule within the ovary. Advanced double fertilisation is omitted.

visual.title: After compatible pollen arrives
visual.description: A pollen grain on the stigma grows a tube through the style towards an ovule. The tube delivers male gametes. A male gamete fuses with an egg cell inside the ovule; the pollen grain itself does not turn into a seed.

elements.text:
Pollen grain grows
a pollen tube

Male gamete
travels through
the tube
One key fusion is shown; advanced double-fertilisation detail omitted.

slides.title: I name what develops into a seed
body: The fertilised ovule develops into a seed.
The ovary develops into fruit.
A pollen grain does not turn into the seed.
slides.notes: Shared I do time. Trace each independent arrow. Ordinary botanical fruits include pods; fruit here is a plant structure, not just a sweet food.

visual.title: Two structures develop after fertilisation
visual.description: Two parallel developmental links: fertilised ovule develops into seed; ovary develops into fruit. The pollen grain is not shown becoming a seed.

elements.text: A seed contains a young plant embryo; fruit surrounds seeds.

slides.title: Orchard evidence desk
body: Use records A–F.
W1. Which record shows pollination?
Which record shows only pollen in the wrong place?
slides.notes: A shows transfer to stigma; D records pollen on leaf. Ask pupils to place or point to the appropriate destination on a diagram.

rows: E: pollen on stigma; inside unseen

slides.title: Audit the missing step
body: W2. Put A, B and C in process order.
Explain what changes from transfer to fusion to development.
slides.notes: A pollination→B fertilisation→C seed/fruit development. A bee does not carry ready-made seeds into the ovary.

slides.title: What does the evidence prove?
body: W3. Record E has pollen on a stigma.
Can the observer claim fertilisation definitely happened?
Give the strongest claim that the record supports.
slides.notes: No; pollen transfer is seen, not gamete fusion. State that the record supports pollination but does not establish later success.
slides.reveal: The record shows pollen on a stigma. It does not by itself prove fertilisation or a mature seed.

slides.title: Which structure becomes a seed?
body: Choose the scientifically accurate explanation.
slides.notes: A false pollen/seed confusion; B correct; C false leaves not seed precursors here.

options.text: The pollen grain simply changes into a seed.
options.feedback: Pollen supplies male gametes; the ovule develops into the seed.

options.text: A fertilised ovule develops into a seed.
options.feedback: This distinguishes reproductive cells from the structure that develops.

options.text: A leaf changes into every seed.
options.feedback: In this model, seeds develop from ovules inside the ovary.

slides.title: Your independent investigation
body: Choose one response route.
Trace the flower-to-seed sequence.
Use records to separate observation from inference.
slides.notes: 10 minutes across the three You do slides. Supply shared page 1 and one selected route page. All routes target the stated science objective; a labelled drawing or independent dictated explanation is valid.

slides.title: Use the evidence
body: Name the destination: anther to stigma.
Distinguish transfer, fusion and development.
State what the observer has actually seen.
slides.notes: Shared You do time. Ask pupils which evidence supports their explanation. Read prompts or scribe without supplying the scientific conclusion.

slides.title: Check before sharing
body: Does my explanation answer the question?
Have I named the evidence or process?
Have I kept the conclusion within its limits?
slides.notes: Shared You do time. Use the route-specific worked answers to identify one precise next step.

slides.title: Compare and improve
body: Share one accurate arrow or process label.
Check it against the source cards.
Improve a seed or fertilisation claim.
slides.notes: 4 minutes across Review. Offer partner or private teacher feedback. Ask for one specific revision linked to evidence; no public ranking.

slides.title: A question worth investigating
body: Suggest one next question about this lesson’s evidence.
Choose a question whose answer would improve our model.
slides.notes: Lundy cycle: invite written, spoken or pointed suggestions. Select one feasible question and explain how the pupil contribution changes the next example or investigation.

slides.title: Show the science you can explain
body: E1. What is pollination?
E2. How is fertilisation different?
E3. What develops into a seed?
slides.notes: Transfer anther→stigma; gamete fusion; fertilised ovule. E4 on pupil page asks why pollen on leaf is insufficient.

pupilPages.title: 1 • Shared evidence: orchard records
pupilPages.intro: These are constructed observation scenarios, not results from a class experiment.

cards.title: A • Transfer event
cards.text: A bee carries pollen from an anther to a stigma of a suitable flower. This is pollen transfer, not the fusion event.

cards.title: B • Inside the flower
cards.text: After compatible pollen arrives, a pollen tube can grow. A male gamete can reach an egg cell in an ovule and fuse with it.

cards.title: C • Development
cards.text: After successful fertilisation, an ovule develops into a seed; the ovary develops into fruit. Other conditions also affect success.

cards.title: D • Wrong destination
cards.text: Pollen is seen on a leaf. No pollen is seen on the stigma in this record. The record does not show pollination.

cards.title: E • Incomplete evidence
cards.text: Pollen is seen on a stigma. The inside of the ovule has not been observed. Pollen transfer alone does not prove fertilisation occurred.

cards.title: F • Model boundary
cards.text: This model follows sexual reproduction in a flowering plant. It omits detailed cell structures and time scales; no class growing experiment took place.

blocks.prompt: W1. Compare records A and D. Which shows pollination?
W2. Order A, B and C and name the three processes.
W3. What can record E establish, and what remains unobserved?

pupilPages.title: 2 • Supported route: follow the pollen
pupilPages.intro: Word bank: anther / stigma / ovule / pollination / fertilisation.

blocks.prompt: S1. Complete the transfer: pollen moves from an ____ to a ____ .
S2. What is that transfer called?
S3. Complete: The fusion of a male gamete and an egg cell is ____ .
S4. Which develops into a seed?
choices: A pollen grain on a leaf

blocks.prompt: S5. Order: seed develops / pollen reaches stigma / gametes fuse. Explain one arrow.
N1. Complete the process table.
N2. Trace pollen’s role from anther to a male gamete reaching an egg cell. Name the ovule.
N3. Explain why pollen on a leaf is not evidence of pollination.
N4. Record E shows pollen on a stigma. Explain what is known and what cannot yet be claimed.

pupilPages.title: 4 • Stretch route: audit the orchard claim
pupilPages.intro: Use precise biological structures and bounded evidence.

blocks.prompt: T1. Explain the full sequence from pollen transfer to seed formation. Include anther, stigma, gamete and ovule.
T2. Repair “Bees carry seeds to a flower, then pollen becomes the fruit”.
T3. Does observing pollen on a stigma guarantee a mature seed? Explain two later requirements or uncertainties.
T4. Design a record that separates observation of pollen arrival from later seed development. What would each observation establish?

pupilPages.title: 5 • Exit and reflection
pupilPages.intro: Use a short explanation or labelled route.

blocks.prompt: E1. What is pollination?
E2. How is fertilisation different?
E3. What develops into a seed, and what develops into fruit?
E4. Why does pollen on a leaf not establish pollination?
Reflection. Which later stage would you investigate next?

answers.label: R1–R3
answers.answer: R1 valid plant part. R2 a new plant in suitable conditions. R3 no; reproduction produces offspring, whereas growth develops an individual.

answers.label: W1–W3
answers.answer: W1 A shows pollination; D has pollen on a leaf, not the required stigma. W2 A→B→C: transfer, fusion, development. W3 pollen on stigma is observed; successful fusion and later seed development are not established by that observation alone.

answers.label: Hinge A–C
answers.answer: A incorrect: pollen does not become seed. B correct. C incorrect: ovules, not leaves, develop into seeds in this model.

answers.label: S1–S5
answers.answer: S1 anther; stigma. S2 pollination. S3 fertilisation. S4 fertilised ovule. S5 pollen reaches stigma→gametes fuse→seed develops; any accurate arrow explanation.

answers.label: N1–N4
answers.answer: N1 pollination: anther-to-stigma transfer; fertilisation: fusion of male/female gametes; seed formation: fertilised ovule develops. N2 pollen arrives at stigma, tube grows and delivers male gamete to egg cell in ovule. N3 leaf is not stigma. N4 transfer is evidenced, not later fertilisation or mature seed success.

answers.label: T1–T4
answers.answer: T1 accurate connected sequence, with distinct transfer and fusion. T2 bees can transfer pollen, not plant seeds into ovaries; ovules develop into seeds and ovaries into fruit. T3 compatible pollen, tube growth/gamete delivery, fertilisation and suitable development conditions remain relevant; choose two without requiring technical detail. T4 separate dated records for pollen arrival on stigma and later seed formation, with a matched observation method; arrival supports pollination, later mature seeds support successful development in the sexual example. A record should not claim unobserved cellular detail.

answers.label: E1–E4 / assessment
answers.answer: E1 transfer anther→stigma. E2 fusion of gametes. E3 ovule→seed, ovary→fruit. E4 incorrect destination. Secure: clear distinction of the three processes and correct structure development. Re-teach by assigning a different verb to each arrow. Reflection has no fixed choice.

teacherNotes: 40 minutes: opening 2; retrieval 3; I do 8; We do 8; hinge 3; You do 10; review 4; exit 2. Zero-minute slides share their stage time.
Supply shared page 1, one selected route page 2, 3 or 4, and page 5. Do not require all three routes. An independent spoken explanation can be recorded verbatim by an adult.
This lesson follows ordinary sexual reproduction in flowering plants; it does not claim every plant seed in nature requires fertilisation. Asexual seed formation is a later teacher nuance.
The interactive uses the same constructed records as W1–W3. Paper pollen tokens provide a complete alternative without exposure to real pollen.

interactive.title: Orchard audit: predict the process
interactive.intro: Predict first, test the model, then explain using the evidence. Move at your own pace; paper W1–W3 tasks assess the same reasoning.
